absent: Locking, serialization and concurrency rules for concurrent traversal, mutation and property updates.
Allocation, reference counting and teardown behaviour of nodes and properties in enabled builds.
Operational semantics of enabled lookup, property decoding, phandle resolution and mapping beyond disabled stubs.
Delivery, ordering and failure handling of reconfiguration notifications.
Bounds, overflow and error handling for iterators, variable-length reads and address translation.

findings.text: Tool annotation tags are small integers: ANNOTYPE_NOENDBR one, ANNOTYPE_RETPOLINE_SAFE two, ANNOTYPE_INSTR_BEGIN three, ANNOTYPE_INSTR_END four, ANNOTYPE_UNRET_BEGIN five, ANNOTYPE_IGNORE_ALTS six, ANNOTYPE_INTRA_FUNCTION_CALL seven, ANNOTYPE_REACHABLE eight, ANNOTYPE_NOCFI nine, and ANNOTYPE_DATA_SPECIAL one.
Lifecycle bit positions: OF_DYNAMIC one, OF_DETACHED two, OF_POPULATED three, OF_POPULATED_BUS four, OF_OVERLAY five, OF_OVERLAY_FREE_CSET six. OF_BAD_ADDR is the all-ones 64-bit value.
Reconfiguration codes: OF_RECONFIG_ATTACH_NODE one, OF_RECONFIG_DETACH_NODE two, OF_RECONFIG_ADD_PROPERTY three, OF_RECONFIG_REMOVE_PROPERTY four, OF_RECONFIG_UPDATE_PROPERTY five.

A property record carries a name pointer, a length, an opaque value pointer and a link to the next property. Builds with dynamic or SPARC support add a flags word; prom-tree builds add a numeric unique identifier; kobject builds add a binary attribute for sysfs exposure.
Numeric handles for firmware nodes are aliases of u32, with separate type names for generic and legacy use. The header is protected by a conventional include guard macro.

A device node record holds name and full-name pointers, a numeric handle, an embedded firmware-node handle, live and removed property lists, parent child and sibling links, a flags word and an opaque driver pointer. Kobject builds embed a kobject; SPARC builds add a unique identifier and an interrupt translation pointer.
A parsed phandle reference bundles a target node pointer, an argument count and a fixed-size array of 32-bit cells. The array bound is defined as equal to NR_FWNODE_REFERENCE_ARGS.

A phandle-list iterator keeps the cells name, expected cell count and parent node, end pointers for the list and current phandle, plus cursor state consisting of current position, current count, resolved handle and resolved node.
Reconfiguration notification data groups the affected node with the new or added property and, for updates, the previous property.
Node initialisation prepares embedded objects: it conditionally initialises the kobject with its node type and always initialises the firmware handle with the device-tree operations.
The kobject accessor has two build variants: one yields the address of the embedded kobject, the other yields null when kobject support is absent.
The reference helpers in this configuration are trivial: acquiring returns its input unchanged and releasing does nothing.

An active firmware handle is recognised by a non-error pointer whose operations match the device-tree operations table. Conversion to a device node derives the enclosing record from the embedded handle when recognised, otherwise null.

A node is a root exactly when its parent link is absent. Flag state lives in a flags word manipulated through atomic bit primitives for test, test-and-set, set and clear. Convenience macros test and set the dynamic bit.
Property flag state, when present, uses the same atomic bit discipline for test, set and clear on its own flags word.

Multi-cell big-endian numbers are decoded by accumulating successive cells from most significant to least, shifting by 32 bits per cell. The unsigned-long helper reuses the 64-bit decode and discards high bits when narrower.

The full-name accessor returns the stored full name, or a fixed no-node marker when absent. All-node iteration repeatedly invokes the global successor helper starting from a given node or from the start.
Path lookup without options delegates to the options-aware path lookup with no options supplied.

When device-tree support is disabled, core initialisation does nothing, firmware-handle recognition always fails, conversion always yields null, name equality and prefix tests always fail, and full-name access always yields a fixed marker.

Disabled builds report absence for every node search and traversal: lookup by name, type, compatible match, path with or without options, handle, or property, and parent, child and sibling stepping including prefixed, available and reserved child variants, all yield null.

Disabled child and compatibility helpers uniformly signal absence: compatible or named child acquisition yields null, compatibility checks yield zero or false, availability and endianness checks yield false, and property search yields null.

Machine compatibility has an enabled wrapper that packages a single string as a one-entry list for the list matcher, while disabled builds report no match. Machine table lookup yields null, its data accessor yields null, and the device-match predicate and matching-node finder build on those primitives.
Presence-style queries report false when disabled: boolean property read and console-node check.

A large family of disabled accessors reports ENOSYS: element counting, indexed and variable-length integer array reads, single and variable 64-bit reads, string read match and helper, phandle parsing mapping and counting, iterator initialisation and stepping, alias identification, and machine model or compatibility string reads, plus NUMA initialisation.
Disabled pointer-returning helpers yield null: raw property access, CPU node acquisition and stepping including state nodes, device match data, and incremental 32-bit and string property cursors.

Some disabled helpers report neutral success values: address and size cell counts are zero, iterator argument extraction succeeds trivially, the integer machine-compatibility check is zero, and property add or remove succeed trivially.

Other disabled helpers use distinct error or sentinel contracts: CPU identifier translation, modalias formatting and module request signal ENODEV; identifier mapping for generic, IOMMU and MSI cases signals EINVAL; maximum DMA address is PHYS_ADDR_MAX; NUMA node translation is NUMA_NO_NODE.
When flag storage is absent, node and property flag helpers are inert: checks and test-and-set report zero and set or clear do nothing.
Match-pointer handling is build-dependent: the enabled variant passes its input through unchanged, the disabled variant yields null, and disabled match-by-node also yields null.
Name comparisons delegate to standard routines, with strcasecmp for compatibility and node names and strcmp for property names.
Device-type access reads the device_type property value, and type testing compares that value for exact equality after null checks.

Property iteration walks the live list via next links. Phandle parsing wrappers delegate to a common argument parser: single-handle lookup requests zero cells and returns the resolved node or null; the general form uses zero when no cells name is given and requests discovery otherwise; the fixed form supplies an explicit count; the optional form supplies zero.

Two parsed references compare equal exactly when target nodes and counts match and the used cell prefix matches. Unsigned element counters for four widths delegate to the sized element counter with their element width.
Core initialisation is the early setup entry that prepares device-tree infrastructure; in disabled builds it is a no-op.

Phandle-list traversal follows an initialise, step, extract discipline: initialisation binds list and cell rules, stepping advances and resolves the next handle and node, and argument extraction copies the current cells.

Tree mutation is announced as one of five transitions such as attach, detach, add, remove and update, carrying the affected node and new versus old property payloads, with lifecycle bits distinguishing dynamic, detached, populated and overlay states.

Disabled-build stubs silently signal absence through null, false, zero or negative codes, so callers must treat those as not-present rather than errors; the bad-address and no-node sentinels and placeholder full-name string must likewise be checked explicitly, and iterator state must not be used after failed initialisation.
External atomic bit test relied upon by flag checks.
External atomic bit set relied upon by flag marking.
External atomic bit clear relied upon by flag clearing.
External atomic test-and-set relied upon by flag acquisition.
